dedupe_keys.name: geo x geospatial commodity production cost model

description: Geo-X models the delivered levelised cost of green hydrogen, green ammonia and green copper for candidate production cells and specified demand locations. Climate Compatible Growth publishes a Snakemake workflow, setup guide and example configurations for Namibia and Zambia. Inputs include H3 spatial cells, renewable weather, plant costs, storage and transport assumptions; copper cases can compare off-grid, hybrid and grid-connected power. Outputs are cost maps and the lowest-cost production routes for the selected commodity and region. Geography is chosen by the modeller, with example country cases. The code is public under MIT terms and supports free solvers such as Cbc. A limitation is that new runs require suitable geographic data and historical weather, for which the guide describes a Climate Data Store API account; this review did not request those data. The model supports hydrogen supply and industrial infrastructure planning. The catalogue's model-pypsa is an underlying optimisation engine, not this geospatial commodity workflow. The older GeoH2 repository directs users to Geo-X as its successor. No model or data file was downloaded.
